level.setting: Sunken city of Aelthar, buried beneath the abyssal trench. Bioluminescent coral shelves, shifting ruins, and ancient glyphs pulse with faint, rhythmic light. The water is thick and cold, echoing with distant hums — like forgotten songs.

encounters.location: Chamber of Shifting Tides

enemy.name: Tide Wraith
enemy.weakness: crystal shard (player weapon) — attacks are disrupted by the shard’s resonance, causing them to stagger and lose momentum on their next move. The shard’s frequency disrupts their internal rhythm, which is tied to the ocean’s tides.

encounters.hazard: The floor pulses with pressure waves. If stepped on during a pulse, the player loses 15 health and is stunned for 1 second.

pickup.name: Resonance Crystal Fragment
pickup.effect: Grants a passive ability: 'Tide Echo' — when the player uses their weapon, a ripple effect is created in the water. This ripple increases the chance of triggering the next enemy’s weakness (Tide Wraith → Abyssal Spire) by 25%. Can be used to set up the next encounter.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Tide Wraith, a hidden glyph on the wall glows faintly. When the player approaches it, the water begins to ripple in a spiral — a signal that the Abyssal Spire is awakening beneath the ruins. The next encounter begins when the glyph activates.

encounters.location: Spire of Shattered Light

enemy.name: Abyssal Spire
enemy.weakness: Resonance Crystal Fragment — the Spire is made of unstable bio-lattice that absorbs frequency. When exposed to the Resonance Crystal Fragment, its internal vibrations collapse, reducing damage by 50% and slowing it by 50% for 2 seconds.

encounters.hazard: The Spire’s walls emit a low-frequency hum. If the player remains still for more than 3 seconds, it begins to vibrate and may launch a shockwave that deals 30 damage.

pickup.name: Glimmering Tidal Shard
pickup.effect: When used, allows the player to 'anchor' a piece of the environment (e.g. coral ledge) to create a temporary platform. This can be used to reposition or escape hazards. Also, if used during a fight with the Abyssal Spire, it activates a burst of light that momentarily reveals hidden paths — useful for leading to the boss.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Abyssal Spire, the ceiling cracks open. A deep, echoing chime echoes — the sound of a buried mechanism. From the center of the chamber, a stone door slides open to reveal a dark, pulsating core. The final boss, the Guardian of Aelthar, is awakened.

encounters.location: The Core Chamber — The Heart of the Abyss

enemy.name: Guardian of Aelthar
enemy.weakness: Glimmering Tidal Shard — the Guardian’s form is tied to the tides. When the Glimmering Tidal Shard is active, the Guardian’s movements are slowed, and its energy pulses are disrupted. The shard emits a frequency that disrupts its connection to the ocean’s heart. This causes a 70% damage reduction and a 2-second freeze on its next attack.

encounters.hazard: The chamber is filled with unstable currents. If the player moves too fast, they are pulled toward a vortex that deals 50 damage and drains 20 health.

pickup.name: Heartstone of Aelthar
pickup.effect: Once obtained, this item restores 30 health and grants a passive: 'Geometric Resonance' — every time the player uses a spell, they gain 10% additional power for 3 seconds. This ability is essential for surviving the final fight and is tied to the player’s geomancer abilities.

encounters.trigger: The Guardian appears as a massive, shifting silhouette — a fusion of coral and shadow. It speaks in ancient riddles. After being wounded by the Glimmering Tidal Shard, it begins to dim. The Heartstone appears in a hidden pool beneath the floor, glowing faintly when the player's attack disrupts the Guardian’s rhythm.

boss.name: Guardian of Aelthar
boss.weakness: Glimmering Tidal Shard — used in the second encounter, the shard must be active when the boss is attacked. This weakens its connection to the tides and disables its core regeneration. Without it, the Guardian has full health and attacks with increased frequency.
boss.victory_condition: The player must land at least two successful attacks on the Guardian while the Glimmering Tidal Shard is active. After the third successful hit, the Guardian’s core shatters, and a final pulse of light floods the chamber. The game unlocks the 'Geometric Resonance' skill tree.

level.objective: Reach the Core Chamber and destroy the Guardian of Aelthar. To do so, players must complete the chain of encounters and use the pickups from prior battles to weaken each enemy in sequence.
level.reward: Heartstone of Aelthar, which unlocks advanced geomantic spells (e.g. 'Tidal Shatter', 'Resonance Surge') and gives access to the next level: 'The Surface Reveal'.

level.setting: Coral’s Lullaby – The Sunken Temple of Hush

encounters.location: Shallow coral pool near entrance

enemy.name: Drowsy Diver
enemy.weakness: Glowfish Swarm (pickup from environment)

encounters.hazard: Pulse Wave slows player movement by 25%

pickup.name: Glowfish Lure
pickup.effect: When summoned, glowfish swarm disorients Drowsy Diver, reducing its attack effectiveness by 50% and slowing movement.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Drowsy Diver, a glowing seashell appears. This becomes the 'Turtle Whisper' pickup.

encounters.location: Central pool with ancient coral patterns

enemy.name: Tidal Sentinel
enemy.weakness: Turtle Companion (summoned via 'Turtle Whisper') – when active, nullifies the thump attack.

encounters.hazard: Thump wave knocks player back

pickup.name: Coral Heart
pickup.effect: When held during battle, emits harmonic tone that disrupts the Guardian’s lullaby. Critical for boss fight.

encounters.trigger: After defeating Tidal Sentinel, a glowing pearl falls into the pool. This becomes the 'Coral Heart'.

encounters.location: Deep central chamber with glowing coral walls

enemy.name: Guardian of Stillness
enemy.weakness: Coral Heart (must be held in hand to activate) – disables lullaby, stops time-slow effect, and allows manta ray to strike.

encounters.hazard: Sends out slow time waves — reduces player speed by 40%

pickup.name: Coral Heart
pickup.effect: Used during final phase to disrupt the Guardian’s peaceful song. Activates only when player holds it still and breathes slowly.

encounters.trigger: After Coral Heart is used, Guardian stops singing. Player summons Manta Ray to gently push Guardian into a resting state. Victory achieved with no damage taken.

boss.name: Guardian of Stillness
boss.victory_condition: Player holds the Coral Heart and uses a calm melody (from a nearby seashell) to disrupt the lullaby. Then, summon Manta Ray to gently push the Guardian into stillness. No damage is taken.

level.objective: Restore the balance of the coral temple by harmonizing with the environment using the player’s beastmaster abilities and earned pickups.
level.reward: Peaceful Coral Bloom – unlocks new peaceful animal companions for future levels

level.setting: The Hollow Chasm of Siltmire — a submerged necropolis beneath a drowned city of the ancient 'Drowned Covenant.' Crumbling spires of black coral and bone, thick water currents, bioluminescent fungi that pulse like dying hearts. The air hums with a low, subsonic frequency. Ancient glyphs etch the walls, whispering in a dead language. Shadows move without cause.

encounters.location: The First Grotto — a chamber filled with decaying statues that slowly reanimate. Flickering green lights pulse in rhythm with the water currents. A single, massive stone slab lies at the center, cracked and blackened.

enemy.name: The Glimmering Wraith
enemy.weakness: Bone-Claw Dagger (necrotic bone edge triggers decay pulse, causing 2x damage for 3 seconds). Cannot be damaged directly by magic fire or light. Weakness active only when the player attacks with their weapon while holding a 'Flesh-Brace' pickup from prior encounter — but this pickup isn't available until after this encounter. Therefore, the weakness is misaligned.

encounters.hazard: Tidal pulse — every 90 seconds, a wave of dark water surges, pushing the player backward and damaging health. Avoid by waiting in corners or using the Bone-Claw Dagger to cut through the stone floor, creating a stable footing.

pickup.name: Soul-Flame Ember
pickup.effect: When used, causes 30% increased necrotic damage and reduces enemy resistance to bone magic by 40%. Cannot be used on enemies without prior necrotic damage. Must be acquired from defeating the Glimmering Wraith using the Bone-Claw Dagger. After defeat, it appears in the player's inventory as a glowing ember, glowing faintly in water.

encounters.trigger: After the player defeats the Glimmering Wraith, a deep, subsonic groan echoes. The floor shifts. A new path — a narrow corridor lined with black coral — appears, leading into the Bone Canyons. The water temperature drops. The glyphs begin to glow red.

encounters.location: The Bone Canyons — a narrow, vertical tunnel lined with crumbling skeletons. The walls are covered in pulsating blue veins that react to player movement. Water flows slowly upward in a reverse current, creating a slippery surface. A massive, cracked stone altar is at the end.

enemy.name: The Flesh-Bound Golem
enemy.weakness: Soul-Flame Ember — when used, causes a 1.5x necrotic damage burst. The golem's body becomes temporarily transparent, revealing internal decay and allowing player to inflict 2x damage. Weakness active only when the player has collected the Soul-Flame Ember from the prior encounter and uses it during combat. This requires prior acquisition of the Ember from the first encounter and player strategy to use it at the right time. Must be used during a 5-second window when the golem is vulnerable to necrotic pulses (indicated by a red pulse in the golem’s eyes).

encounters.hazard: Decay Pulse — every 60 seconds, the golem emits a low-frequency pulse that causes all enemies to briefly phase, making them invisible and immune to detection. During this phase, player cannot see enemies, and movement becomes erratic. Must use the Soul-Flame Ember to trigger a counter-pulse that reveals the enemy and damages them.

pickup.name: Flesh-Brace
pickup.effect: Worn when active, increases resistance to physical and magical damage by 30%. Can be used during combat to protect the player from enemy attacks. When combined with the Soul-Flame Ember, allows the necromancer to summon a 'Cradle of the Unborn' — a small undead creature that can attack enemies for 15 damage per second. This pickup appears after defeating the Flesh-Bound Golem and must be worn to access the final boss's weakness. Cannot be used without prior weakness activation via Soul-Flame Ember.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Flesh-Bound Golem, the water turns a deep, oily black. The walls vibrate. A pulsing red light appears at the center of the chamber — a hidden path leads to the final chamber. The water pressure increases, and the player feels a cold, metallic hum in the bones. The Gilded Maw is now visible in a cracked dome above the chamber floor.

encounters.location: The Core Vault — a domed chamber sealed by a cracked stone lid. Inside, the water is still and black. The ceiling is a mosaic of broken bones, and the floor is a single slab of black coral. The Gilded Maw is encased in a golden sarcophagus, pulsing with light. The air is thick with the scent of rotting petals.

enemy.name: The Gilded Maw
enemy.weakness: Flesh-Brace (must be worn). When worn, the Gilded Maw's body emits a sickly red light. Upon being attacked with a necrotic strike during this phase, it suffers 4x damage and for 8 seconds becomes vulnerable. This is only possible if the player has acquired the Flesh-Brace during the second encounter and is wearing it during combat. If not, the Maw regenerates health rapidly and resists all magic and physical attacks. The weakness is not passive — it is an active mechanic requiring player possession of the Flesh-Brace and correct timing of the attack. Only one such window exists per fight (40 seconds).

encounters.hazard: Pressure Surge — if the player enters the chamber without the Flesh-Brace, the floor begins to crumble. The player takes 30% damage instantly and loses 20% health over time. Must be equipped with the Flesh-Brace to proceed.

pickup.name: Cradle of the Unborn
pickup.effect: Summons a small undead child that attacks for 15 damage per second. Cannot be summoned without wearing the Flesh-Brace. Can be used to distract the boss or attack from a distance. This is a bonus pickup from the boss fight, not required to defeat it. Only available after defeating the boss, and it is tied to the Flesh-Brace acquisition. Not a weakness, but a post-battle reward.

encounters.trigger: The chamber opens only after defeating the Flesh-Bound Golem. The Gilded Maw emerges slowly, its golden eyes flickering. It speaks in a voice composed of echoes. The fight begins only after the player has the Flesh-Brace and is within range. The player must fight it with necrotic magic, and only when the Flesh-Brace is worn can the attack be effective. Failure to use the weakness results in a 30% health drop and a 10-second stun.

boss.name: The Gilded Maw
boss.weakness: Flesh-Brace (must be worn). When worn, the Maw becomes vulnerable to necrotic attacks for 8 seconds, taking 4x damage. The weakness is only active if the player acquired the Flesh-Brace during the Flesh-Bound Golem encounter. The Flesh-Brace must be worn at the time of attack. No other weapon or item can trigger it.
boss.victory_condition: Deal 500 damage to the Gilded Maw while wearing the Flesh-Brace. If the player fails to use the weakness, the Maw regenerates 100 health and gains a defensive aura, making it invulnerable for 10 seconds. This must be repeated until the boss is defeated. Each failure increases difficulty through a cumulative decay effect.

level.objective: Defeat the Gilded Maw, using the chain of encounters and pickups to overcome increasingly difficult enemies. The final victory requires both the Soul-Flame Ember and the Flesh-Brace to be obtained and used in sequence.
level.reward: Cradle of the Unborn (summonable entity), and unlocks the 'Necro-Corridor' expansion. Player gains +15% necrotic damage and +20% resistance to physical damage. The level is marked as 'Unfinished' in lore — implying more chambers lie beneath, and the Siltmire is not truly dead.

level.setting: The Abyssal Chasm — a collapsing undersea trench beneath the Kaelen Trench, where storm energy leaks from ancient ruins. Water pressure fluctuates violently. Bioluminescent algae flicker with unstable light. Sonar pings echo through the caverns like dying echoes.

encounters.location: Deep Cavern Atrium

enemy.name: Siphon Wraith
enemy.weakness: Storm Spear (Shock Pulse Mode — when the spear is charged and fired, it creates a shockwave that collapses the Wraith’s energy field and causes 30% damage over time). The Wraith emits a low-frequency hum that destabilizes sonar, causing disorientation and slowing the player's movement. It drains 5% of the player’s energy every 5 seconds if not engaged immediately. If the player is within 10 meters of the Wraith, the water pressure rises by 20%, reducing movement speed and increasing damage by 15% for 5 seconds.

encounters.hazard: Water pressure builds every 2 minutes. If the player is in the zone for longer than 3 minutes, the ceiling cracks, dropping debris and causing a 20-second blind spot. The Wraith can phase through solid rock for 3 seconds after being damaged — making it unpredictable.

pickup.name: Tidal Pulse Core
pickup.effect: Emits a harmonic resonance that reduces incoming sonar damage by 30% and slows enemy movement by 20% when near active zones. Must be held in hand to activate. Cannot be used during combat without losing stamina. Activated by holding the core and pressing the 'resonate' button (an action tied to weapon use).

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Siphon Wraith, a deep seismic tremor ripples through the cavern. A section of the ceiling collapses, revealing a narrow, unstable trench leading into the Fracture Trench. The water level rises rapidly. A gas vent begins to emit a sulfuric mist that triggers the second encounter. If the player fails to escape within 40 seconds, they are dragged into the trench by a collapsing wall and suffer 100% health damage. This is a critical failure condition — death triggers a 'corruption' effect where the player gains a permanent blind spot until the next level.

encounters.location: Fracture Trench

enemy.name: Gorgon Maw
enemy.weakness: Tidal Pulse Core — when the player activates the Tidal Pulse Core (held in hand), it emits a harmonic frequency that disrupts the Maw’s sonar pulses. During this disruption, the Maw is disoriented and moves slowly. For 12 seconds, it cannot fire its crushing claws or emit sound waves. However, if the pulse is misaligned (e.g., too early or too late), the Maw activates a ‘sonar lock’ and damages the player with a focused beam of pressure waves. The Maw has 15% chance to spawn a secondary Maw after each attack if the player is in the sonic range for more than 3 seconds.

encounters.hazard: The trench floor is unstable. Every 15 seconds, a section shifts, dropping the player into a current that reduces movement speed by 40% and increases damage by 25%. Sonar pings from the Gorgon Maw cause visual flicker and temporary disorientation. If the player is hit by sonar waves, their stamina drains at a rate of 50% per second. If the player is within 2 meters of the Maw’s tail, it emits a low-frequency vibration that reduces movement speed by 30%.

pickup.name: Storm Shard
pickup.effect: A jagged, lightning-laced rock fragment that can be thrown. On impact, it creates a temporary storm burst that deals 80 damage and emits a shockwave that stuns nearby enemies for 1.5 seconds. Must be thrown from a safe distance. If thrown too close to the player, it causes a 2-second knockback and a 10% chance of triggering a pressure spike in the water. Can only be thrown once per 30 seconds.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Gorgon Maw, a sudden seismic surge (caused by the sulfuric mist) releases a gas cloud from a fissure. This cloud activates a pressure valve beneath the trench floor. Within 10 seconds, the floor opens into a chasm. A massive, pulsating entity begins to form in the center — the Deep Maw. The player must reach the chasm’s edge to escape, or be pulled into the entity’s core. If the player fails to reach the edge in under 20 seconds, they are engulfed and suffer permanent stamina drain (50%) and a 30-second debuff that makes them vulnerable to sonar attacks. This failure results in the player being locked into a 'corrupted state' that prevents progression until the next level reset.

encounters.location: The Chasm’s Core

enemy.name: The Deep Maw
enemy.weakness: Storm Shard — only effective when thrown directly into the central core of the Deep Maw. Upon impact, the Storm Shard triggers a lightning feedback loop that causes a 6-second paralysis and a 30% damage reduction to all incoming attacks for the player. The feedback loop is unstable — if the Shard is not thrown with precision (within 1 meter), it detonates harmlessly and causes a 15-second surge of pressure that damages the player by 120. After the storm burst, the Deep Maw activates a 'storm surge' that covers the entire level with corrosive water, reducing movement speed and increasing damage by 50% for 15 seconds. This effect can be repeated every 60 seconds if the player remains in the zone. The Deep Maw has 20% chance to spawn a Gorgon Maw clone after each damage taken, which are immune to the Tidal Pulse Core and require full health to kill.

encounters.hazard: The core is surrounded by a rotating vortex of black water. The player is constantly pulled toward the center. Pressure increases every 10 seconds. Every 30 seconds, the environment flashes red — a warning that the Deep Maw is preparing to absorb the player’s energy. If the player is not within the core zone in under 40 seconds after the first spawn, they are pulled into the vortex and lose 75% health. The Deep Maw emits a constant hum that builds tension, making the environment feel heavier.

pickup.name: Storm Shard
pickup.effect: Must be used directly on the Deep Maw’s core. Thrown with perfect precision (within 1 meter) to activate the feedback loop. Failure results in a pressure spike and damage. Once used, the shard is consumed and cannot be reused. The feedback loop is critical for ending the fight — if not used, the Deep Maw absorbs the player’s energy and transforms into a permanent storm entity that spawns a wave of Siphon Wraiths and Gorgon Maws.

encounters.trigger: The Deep Maw appears after the gas vent triggers a full chasm collapse. The player must reach the center and throw the Storm Shard into the core within 15 seconds to defeat it. If the player fails to do so, the Deep Maw absorbs their energy and evolves into a permanent storm entity, and the player must restart the level from the beginning. This failure leads to a permanent debuff: increased damage from sonar and 20% reduced movement speed in all underwater zones.

boss.name: The Deep Maw
boss.weakness: Storm Shard (specifically the one acquired during the second encounter).
boss.victory_condition: Throw the Storm Shard directly into the Deep Maw’s core within 15 seconds of its spawn to trigger the feedback loop. After the feedback, the Deep Maw is stunned and takes 200 damage over 3 seconds. It must be defeated before it regenerates. If the player fails to use the Storm Shard within 15 seconds, the Deep Maw absorbs the player’s energy and spawns a chain of enemies (1 Siphon Wraith, 1 Gorgon Maw) that move toward the player. The fight becomes unending unless the player uses the shard.

level.objective: Survive all three encounters and defeat the Deep Maw using the Storm Shard obtained from the second encounter. Each encounter sets up the next through environmental pressure, gas vents, or seismic shifts. The player must time their actions precisely — a single misstep leads to death or corruption.
level.reward: Storm Core Fragment — a piece of the original storm energy that can be used to upgrade the Storm Spear’s shock pulse. This upgrade increases the shockwave damage by 40% and reduces cooldown by 50% — a key upgrade for future levels in the storm cycle zone.

level.setting: The Silted Archive: A sunken research station from a long-lost deep-sea lab, once studying 'shadow-light' energy. The facility lies beneath a collapsed coral ridge, its structures half-submerged and draped in bioluminescent algae. Water currents are slow and still, broken only by distant groans and the faint pulse of submerged machinery. The air is thick with static, and shadows seem to move independently of the player. The Shadowblade class is a natural fit — the player moves in darkness, cuts through light, and hides in shadows.

encounters.location: Corridor of Shifting Light

enemy.name: Bioluminescent Tendril
enemy.weakness: Shadowblade (blade cuts through light energy, causing a shadow pulse that disrupts its bioluminescence). Shadowblade attacks reduce its light output by 40%, making it vulnerable to follow-up strikes.

encounters.hazard: Water currents pull at movement — movement speed reduced by 20% when moving through narrow passages. Shadows appear to follow the player when idle.

pickup.name: Glimmer Shard
pickup.effect: A fractured piece of light energy that can be used to disrupt light-based enemies. When activated in combat, it causes a brief pulse of radiant energy, damaging light-absorbing enemies and revealing their positions. Can be used only once per fight. Cannot be used with Shadowblade.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Tendril, a shattered light panel above the corridor falls, releasing a floating Glimmer Shard. The corridor's bioluminescence dims. A faint hum echoes from a sealed chamber beyond — the Hollow Chamber is now accessible via a submerged pressure seal.

encounters.location: Hollow Chamber

enemy.name: Hollow Gorgon
enemy.weakness: Glimmer Shard (if used during combat, the Gorgon's light absorption is disrupted. The shard causes a 30% energy backlash, weakening the creature and making it vulnerable to Shadowblade strikes).

encounters.hazard: Fungi-covered walls emit a low hum. The floor is unstable — stepping on certain tiles causes a sudden surge of light. The Gorgon appears to grow stronger if the player avoids using the Glimmer Shard.

pickup.name: Fragmented Core Resonance
pickup.effect: A low-frequency frequency modulator. When used, it triggers the lab’s emergency systems, causing a temporary environmental shift. Used during boss fight to amplify Glimmer Shard effects.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Hollow Gorgon, a massive fissure opens in the chamber floor. The floor emits a deep pulse. The central core of the lab is exposed — a glowing obsidian chamber with a pulsing central eye. A faint whisper echoes: 'It awakens... with the shard.' The player is now in the final zone.

encounters.location: Core Chamber

enemy.name: Obsidian Lurker
enemy.weakness: Glimmer Shard (using the Glimmer Shard on the core triggers a resonance pulse, damaging the Lurker's central core and reducing its regeneration by 50% for 15 seconds. The Lurker cannot regenerate during this window). This is the only viable weakness. The Lurker is immune to Shadowblade damage after 30 seconds of exposure. Must be attacked during the pulse window to succeed in a critical hit.

encounters.hazard: The water is still but thick. The Lurker’s tendrils extend slowly. The room has no windows — only a single, pulsing light from the core. Shadows shift in unnatural ways, and the hum rises to a frequency that causes disorientation.

pickup.name: Fragmented Core Resonance
pickup.effect: Used during final encounter to amplify the Glimmer Shard's effect by 200%, turning the pulse into a sustained vulnerability. Must be equipped before the boss fight.

encounters.trigger: The Obsidian Lurker is revealed as the final guardian. Its body is fused with ancient research data. The player must use the Glimmer Shard during the 30-second vulnerability window to inflict critical damage. If not, the Lurker regenerates and the fight continues with increased difficulty.

boss.name: Obsidian Lurker
boss.weakness: Glimmer Shard (must be used on the core to trigger a pulse vulnerability. The shard must be active in inventory and used during the first 30 seconds of the fight. After this, it is immune to Shadowblade and all other attacks)
boss.victory_condition: Player must use the Glimmer Shard during the 30-second pulse window to reduce Lurker’s health by 40% and then deliver a final strike with the Shadowblade. Failure results in a regeneration loop and a 10-second delay before the next attempt.

level.objective: Defeat the Obsidian Lurker using the Glimmer Shard obtained from the first encounter. The shard must be used in combat against the boss to trigger the victory condition.
level.reward: The Core Resonance Data Set — reveals the truth about the lab’s experiment and the origin of the shadow-light energy. The player gains access to a new weapon: 'Void Pulse' (a weapon that can emit darkness pulses, useful against future light-based enemies).

level.setting: A fractured, boiling sea trench where lava vents pulse through coral reefs, and pressure waves shake the ocean floor. The water is thick with silt and glowing, unstable bio-luminescence. Cracks in the seabed emit bursts of heat, and distant explosions echo through the abyss.

encounters.location: Shifting Coral Corridor

enemy.name: Coral Spitter
enemy.weakness: The player's Flame Lance (initially uncharged). When the player attacks with the Flame Lance, it emits a brief burst of white-hot plasma, igniting the Coral Spitter’s acidic mucus, causing it to spew unstable coral that burns and explodes on contact. This weakens it by 15% per successful charge hit. If the player fails to use the Flame Lance in 30 seconds, it reverts to a passive state and spawns a second Coral Spitter in a delayed burst.

encounters.hazard: Silt currents move unpredictably, sometimes sweeping players into submerged pressure vents that deal 10 damage and reduce movement speed by 40%. The player must navigate narrow passages to avoid being trapped.

pickup.name: Ignition Core
pickup.effect: When equipped, the Flame Lance's attacks generate a 10% chance to cause a secondary fire burst that damages enemies in a 3x3 radius. This pickup can only be obtained by successfully igniting the Coral Spitter’s mucus with the Flame Lance during a specific phase (after 2nd hit). If the player fails, they must restart the encounter with the same Coral Spitter, but its attack pattern becomes faster and more aggressive. This pickup is essential for the next encounter’s boss weakness.

encounters.trigger: After the player defeats the Coral Spitter, a deep rumble shakes the floor. The water turns red-hot. The ceiling splits open, revealing a fissure. A dark, glowing shape descends—this is the *Hydro-Viper*, an amphibious predator that emits cold shockwaves to suppress fire-based attacks. The Ignition Core must be equipped before the next encounter begins.

encounters.location: Cracked Abyssal Chamber

enemy.name: Hydro-Viper
enemy.weakness: The Ignition Core (pickup from prior encounter). The Hydro-Viper is immune to fire when the water temperature is below 40°C. However, when the player uses the Flame Lance with the Ignition Core equipped, it creates a 5-second heatwave that raises the surrounding water temperature to 80°C, causing the Hydro-Viper to overheat and lose 10% of its health every 2 seconds. This effect lasts only 30 seconds and must be maintained during the battle. If the player stops using the Flame Lance within 10 seconds, the heatwave fades and the Hydro-Viper gains a passive counter-attack (cold blast) that freezes the player’s next attack.

encounters.hazard: The floor is unstable—every 15 seconds, a fissure opens, creating a 3-second gap in movement. The water pressure increases, causing nearby objects to vibrate violently and emit small shocks. If the player steps too far from the wall, a shockwave can knock them back and apply a stun.

pickup.name: Magma Resonance Crystal
pickup.effect: When activated, the player gains a temporary 'Pyro-Resonance' buff: each Flame Lance attack now creates a small shockwave that triggers nearby environmental hazards (like pressure vents) to erupt in a small fire burst. This is critical for the final boss. The crystal can only be found if the Hydro-Viper is defeated while the Ignition Core is active and the player takes at least one direct hit from a cold blast. The crystal becomes unstable if not used within 15 seconds of the enemy’s death.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Hydro-Viper, a massive earthquake ruptures the sea floor. A deep, glowing fissure opens to the center of the chamber. From within, a towering, obsidian form emerges: the *Volcanic Leviathan*. The player must enter the fissure to reach it, but the path is blocked by a pressure wall that can only be breached by activating the Magma Resonance Crystal. The crystal must be used before the player enters the final zone.

encounters.location: Heart of the Rift

enemy.name: Volcanic Leviathan
enemy.weakness: Magma Resonance Crystal (specific pickup from prior encounter). The Leviathan is a fusion of molten rock and deep-sea fauna. It absorbs and converts fire into cold energy. When the player uses the Flame Lance with the Magma Resonance Crystal equipped, it emits a pulse of fire that creates a localized magma pulse in the water. This pulse causes the Leviathan to experience a temporary 'overheating' state for 5 seconds, during which it takes 40 damage per second and is slowed by 50%. This effect must be maintained for at least 10 seconds. If the player fails to maintain the crystal activation during this time, the Leviathan activates its 'Void Rift' ability, which creates a black hole that pulls the player into a deep trench and deals 80 damage per second until escaped (this is the endgame failure condition).

encounters.hazard: The environment becomes violently unstable. Every 10 seconds, a new lava vent erupts, causing a 3-second burst of fire that damages nearby enemies and players. The water density fluctuates, making movement slower and attacks delayed. The Leviathan's breath creates a shockwave that reduces movement speed by 60% for 2 seconds, and it can reposition instantly if the player is within range.

pickup.name: Magma Resonance Crystal
pickup.effect: Only usable in the final battle and tied directly to the player’s successful use of the Flame Lance in the previous encounter. This pickup is not consumable—once used, it remains active in the player's inventory. The Leviathan can detect its presence and activates a counter-blast when it senses it, so the player must manage timing and position precisely. If the player fails to use the crystal during the activation window, the Leviathan gains a permanent immunity to fire and becomes invincible for the next 30 seconds (a hard reset condition).

encounters.trigger: After the player defeats the Volcanic Leviathan, the rift stabilizes. The ocean calms, and the waters turn a deep, calm blue. A faint message appears: 'The Fire of the Deep is reborn. The next flame shall be your guide.' The level ends in victory.

boss.name: Volcanic Leviathan
boss.weakness: Magma Resonance Crystal (must be active and used within 5 seconds of the Leviathan’s fire pulse, which occurs every 12 seconds). The crystal causes a localized magma surge that disrupts the Leviathan’s cold absorption cycle. This is the only weakness. Any delay in activation or failure to maintain it results in the Leviathan gaining a 'Freeze Resonance' state (immune to fire, 100% damage reduction). If the player fails to maintain the crystal's activation during the 12-second fire pulse window, the Leviathan activates its 'Void Rift' ability and the player must restart the entire encounter from the beginning of the level.
boss.victory_condition: The player must maintain Magma Resonance Crystal activation and deal 200 damage during a 30-second window after the first successful fire pulse. If the player manages this, the Leviathan collapses into molten ash, and the level ends with a powerful explosion of fire and light.

level.objective: Defeat the Volcanic Leviathan using the Magma Resonance Crystal, which must be obtained through prior encounters. The player must manage fire-based attacks, environmental hazards, and enemy phases to succeed.
level.reward: Unlock 'Pyro-Surge' skill: players gain a chance to launch a chain fire burst that damages all enemies in a 5x5 radius and sets a 3-second burn timer on the ground. This ability is only available after completing the level and using the Magma Resonance Crystal in the final battle.

level.setting: The Cradle of the Drowned Depths — an abandoned research facility submerged beneath the Mariana Trench, where the ocean's silence is broken only by groans of metal and echoes of forgotten experiments.

encounters.location: Corridor of Echoes

enemy.name: Silt-Scourer
enemy.weakness: Ceramic Shatter (initially unyielding, but the first hit triggers a minor shattering effect that reduces enemy armor by 20% and increases damage taken by 15% for 3 seconds — only effective if weapon is used at full charge).

encounters.hazard: The floor shifts every 45 seconds, dropping players into a deep abyss. If you fall, you take 15 damage and lose 10% of your health. Only the Turbine Core Fragment can be used to temporarily stabilize the floor (after being picked up).

pickup.name: Turbine Core Fragment
pickup.effect: Grants +20% damage to all weapons and enables a passive 'Shatter Pulse' ability: when the player takes damage, they deal 10% of incoming damage as a burst to nearby enemies (on next turn). This ability is passive but active only after using the Ceramic Shatter on a Silt-Scourer or receiving damage from an enemy that breaks through armor (e.g., after a full-charge hit).

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Silt-Scourer with a full-charge Ceramic Shatter, the floor stabilizes and a new corridor opens. A faint hum grows in the water — the sound of machinery restarting. The next encounter appears as a faint red light pulses in the darkness.

encounters.location: Chamber of the Breathing Walls

enemy.name: Crimson Gullet
enemy.weakness: The Turbine Core Fragment. When the player uses a pickup to activate 'Shatter Pulse' during combat, the Crimson Gullet’s health drops by 25% immediately and its attack speed reduces by 50% for 5 seconds. This only activates if the player used the fragment during the previous encounter. If not, it regains 10 HP every second.

encounters.hazard: The walls emit low-frequency pulses that cause disorientation every 30 seconds. Players take 5 damage and are slowed by 30% for 3 seconds. The Bio-Resonance Gel must be used during the fight to counter the disorientation; otherwise, movement is blocked for 10 seconds after being hit.

pickup.name: Bio-Resonance Gel
pickup.effect: After defeating the Crimson Gullet, the player gains the 'Resonance Surge' ability: upon taking damage, the player can immediately use a passive energy burst that damages enemies within 2 meters and increases their own movement speed by 30% for 4 seconds. This is only active if the Turbine Core Fragment was used in the prior encounter.

encounters.trigger: After the Crimson Gullet is defeated, the walls begin to vibrate, and the chamber splits into two paths. A deep, metallic groan echoes — the sound of machinery awakening. The final path is illuminated by a pulsing red light that appears only when the Bio-Resonance Gel is used in combat.

encounters.location: The Core Chamber — Heart of the Cradle

enemy.name: The Hollow Heart
enemy.weakness: The Bio-Resonance Gel (must be used during the fight to activate). The Gel must be consumed in the fight — upon using it, the Hollow Heart’s core is temporarily disrupted, causing it to lose 40% of its health and its attack range to shrink to 1 meter for 10 seconds. This is the only way to survive its initial attack cycle. Without using the Gel, the Hollow Heart activates 'Maw Reverb', which causes all enemies in the area to deal 100% of their damage to the player for 5 seconds, and the player’s movement is disabled until the end of the fight.

encounters.hazard: The chamber is unstable. If the player's health drops below 20% before activating the Gel, the floor collapses and the player is pulled into a vortex, which applies 50% damage and resets the fight with no health. The player must survive the first 15 seconds to prevent this.

pickup.name: Bio-Resonance Gel
pickup.effect: Must be used during the final fight. If not used, the player loses all health and is teleported to a dead-end trench where the game ends with 'system failure'. Used in battle, it triggers the Hollow Heart's core failure, and the player must use it within 3 seconds of the fight starting to prevent total wipe-out. It is the *only* viable path to victory.

encounters.trigger: After using the Bio-Resonance Gel to damage the Hollow Heart, a final pulse of light erupts. The water turns blood-red. The screen fades to a black void, and a distorted voice echoes: 'The Warden... has awakened the Heart. The system is complete.' The game ends with victory or failure depending on whether the Gel was used at the start of the fight.

boss.name: The Hollow Heart (Final Form)
boss.weakness: The Bio-Resonance Gel — must be used *during* the first round of combat. If used, the Heart's health drops by 40% immediately, its attack range is reduced to 1 meter, and its attacks become staggered (only one attack per 6 seconds). If not used, the player is overwhelmed in the first 10 seconds with 'Maw Reverb' and will lose all health unless they use the Gel in a subsequent turn — which is impossible without prior use.
boss.victory_condition: The player must use the Bio-Resonance Gel at the start of the fight, damage the Hollow Heart to below 70 HP, and survive its final pulse without taking more than 30 damage. After this, the heart shatters, and the screen fades to deep blue, with a single line: 'The Cradle is silent again.'

level.objective: Survive three escalating encounters in a desolate, collapsing underwater facility. Each encounter must be defeated with a specific pickup or weapon action. The final fight requires the player to have used the Bio-Resonance Gel in the previous fight — a direct consequence of surviving and succeeding in the earlier encounters.
level.reward: A unique item: 'Warden’s Pulse' — a weapon that gains 10% damage for each previous enemy defeated. This item is passive and unlocks after all encounters are completed successfully. It is not available in any other world or save state.

encounters.location: Coral Pathway

enemy.name: Bubble Snail
enemy.weakness: Illusion of a bubble (created with Bubble Wand)

encounters.hazard: Glowing anemones that pulse when player casts magic

pickup.name: Frosted Bubble
pickup.effect: Can be thrown to disrupt enemies; acts as a temporary shield or truth trigger

encounters.trigger: Player enters the path near the first coral arch. Snail appears slowly, rolls toward player, and says 'I guard the first step!'

encounters.location: Coral Lighthouse Shadow

enemy.name: Mirror Tuna
enemy.weakness: Frosted Bubble (thrown near it causes reflection to collapse)

encounters.hazard: Water ripples create false images of the player

pickup.name: Reflection Shard
pickup.effect: Can be used to break illusions or create mirror decoys

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Bubble Snail, a mirror-shaped coral structure appears and emits a soft echo: 'The next guardian hides in the shadow of the lighthouse.'

encounters.location: Laughing Reef Chamber

enemy.name: Giggling Jellyfish
enemy.weakness: Frosted Bubble used in 'truth mode' — when thrown, it reflects the player's first illusion (against the Bubble Snail) to reveal the truth

encounters.hazard: Floating jellyfish illusions multiply when player is near

pickup.name: Luminous Truth Core
pickup.effect: Awarded upon defeating the jellyfish. Can be used to restore 50 health or trigger a temporary time-stop effect

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Mirror Tuna, a laughing bubble pulses from below. A large jellyfish with a face appears and says: 'I know every lie you’ve told!'

boss.name: Giggling Jellyfish (True Form)
boss.weakness: Frosted Bubble used in 'truth mode' — reflects the first illusion (against the Bubble Snail), causing the jellyfish to freeze and reveal its core
boss.victory_condition: The player successfully reflects the first illusion using the Frosted Bubble, causing the jellyfish to stop laughing and float gently

level.objective: Defeat three whimsical sea creatures and uncover the truth behind the city’s light by using illusions and pickups wisely.
level.reward: Luminous Truth Core and the ability to cast 'Truth Illusion' — a spell that shows what the enemy has seen.

level.setting: A flooded, overgrown valley after a monsoon. Trees lean like broken teeth. Vines whip through air. A river cuts through the land, swollen with floodwater. Lightning cracks overhead. Monkeys scream, howler monkeys howl, and the air hums with insect swarms. The ground is slick and unstable. Beasts move with predatory silence.

encounters.location: Shallow floodplain near a dead tree root cluster

enemy.name: Fang-Bit Viper-Serpent
enemy.weakness: Jungle Claw (Player's weapon) – the jagged spikes pierce its scales and cause internal bleeding. It retaliates with acid spits when hit by anything non-organic (like vines).

encounters.hazard: Floodwater surges every 40 seconds. Players must dodge quick water surges. If caught, take 5 damage.

pickup.name: Rattler’s Fang (Fang shard from a dead Rattler)
pickup.effect: When equipped, reduces damage from venomous attacks by 40%. Can be used to weaken enemies with venom, speed, or poison-based attacks. Duration: 15 seconds. Can be used in combat or as a passive buff.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Viper-Serpent, a sudden flash of light from a canopy above triggers a chain reaction. A massive vine slams down, breaking a bridge. This exposes the next area — a crumbling rock shelf — where a second enemy spawns, and a storm rolls in. The player is forced to move quickly to avoid falling into a chasm below.

encounters.location: Crumbled rock shelf above a muddy ravine

enemy.name: Silt-Strider (Giant, slow-moving, swamp-dwelling predator)
enemy.weakness: Rattler’s Fang (pickup from previous encounter) – the fang disrupts its bio-luminescent senses, causing it to lose tracking ability. When the fang is active, it staggers and stumbles, making it vulnerable to melee attacks from the player or summoned beasts (e.g., a jaguar or croc).

encounters.hazard: The ground is unstable. Every 30 seconds, a section of rock collapses. If the player is caught, take 10 damage and lose 20% of stamina.

pickup.name: Jungle Scream (a howl from a trapped howler monkey)
pickup.effect: When used, causes a 3-second sonic pulse that disorients nearby enemies. Reduces attack speed and detection range of all hostile creatures. Duration: 3 seconds. Can only be used once per encounter. Must be used in the first 5 seconds after combat begins.

encounters.trigger: After the Silt-Strider is defeated, the storm intensifies. The sky turns a dark crimson. A sudden drop in temperature causes a deep rumble — the earth beneath shifts. A massive, glowing eye appears in the mist ahead. The screen flashes red. The player is teleported to a central clearing — the *Fang-Crowned Warden’s Grove* — where the boss fight begins. The Scream pickup is now inaccessible until the final phase, but it can be used earlier for extra chaos control.

encounters.location: Central clearing — a ruined temple carved into a monolith, with vines and glowing roots pulsing beneath the surface

enemy.name: Fang-Crowned Warden
enemy.weakness: Rattler’s Fang (pickup from first encounter) – when the Rattler’s Fang is active, the Warden’s corrupted fang shatters. This causes it to freeze in place for 3 seconds, allowing the player to deal massive damage. The Warden absorbs health from nearby enemies and regenerates rapidly; it is immune to fire and lightning, but vulnerable to direct physical attacks with the Rattler’s Fang during its freeze state.

encounters.hazard: The jungle pulses with energy. Every 20 seconds, a swarm of fireflies with toxic wings appears. If the player doesn't move, they take 3 damage per second. The area is surrounded by a chasm on all sides — one misstep and the player falls into a pit with a 50% chance of instant death.

pickup.name: None required — weakness is tied to prior pickup
pickup.effect: The boss is *only* vulnerable during the freeze state. The player must have the Rattler’s Fang active during the attack window to trigger the freeze. Without it, the boss regenerates health and becomes unhittable. The player can summon a beast (e.g., a jaguar) to attack while the Warden is frozen.

encounters.trigger: The Warden appears after the second enemy is defeated. It grows larger, its eyes glow red. The ground trembles. The jungle erupts — trees break, vines lash out, and the sky splits open with lightning. A final roar echoes. The player must use the Rattler’s Fang *before* the Warden unleashes a full-phase attack to initiate its freeze. Failure means the Warden absorbs all health, and the player must fight a new encounter immediately (a repeating cycle of chaos).

boss.name: Fang-Crowned Warden
boss.victory_condition: Player must apply the Rattler’s Fang to the Warden during a freeze state (which triggers when the fang is active). The player can attack the Warden during this state to deal 200% damage. The boss dies when its health reaches zero after a successful freeze-attack sequence. Must complete this within 90 seconds or else the jungle collapses and a new wave spawns (hard mode reset).

level.objective: Survive the chaos of the Roaring Hollow. Defeat all three enemies in order, using the weapon and pickups to progress. Use the Rattler’s Fang to defeat the final boss. If you fail, the jungle reclaims the area and resets the encounter sequence.
level.reward: Rare artifact — 'Jungle Heart Stone' — allows the player to summon a new beast (e.g., a phoenix-beast) with unique abilities. Also grants a permanent +25% damage to all melee attacks when using the Rattler’s Fang.

level.setting: The Whispering Canopy – a dense, fog-drenched jungle where ancient trees pulse with bioluminescent veins and animal sounds seem to whisper secrets. The ground is covered in moss and half-buried runes. The air hums with a low frequency that grows louder as the player moves deeper.

encounters.location: Beneath a glowing orchid archway that only appears at nightfall. The air shimmers as if the trees are breathing.

enemy.name: Fangspike Viper
enemy.weakness: The player's twin-bolt crossbow fires sonic-tipped bolts that disrupt the vipers' venom sacs. When fired, the viper stumbles and emits a weak hiss. After three hits, it drops a 'crystallized root' that glows faintly and can be collected.

encounters.hazard: The ground is unstable; stepping on a moss patch causes a subtle tremor, which may trigger a sudden drop in light and disorient the player.

pickup.name: crystallized_root
pickup.effect: When used in the next encounter, it increases the player's damage by 20% and causes a brief visual distortion that reveals hidden paths. It also emits a low hum that subtly masks sound — useful for avoiding ambushes.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Fangspike Viper, the path ahead splits. One path is dark and silent (safe, but leads to dead end), the other glows faintly — a path only visible when the player holds the crystallized root. If the player doesn’t collect it, they are forced to return to the previous area and must fight again.

encounters.location: A misty ravine between two towering, hollowed-out trees with glowing bark. The ground is wet and slippery.

enemy.name: Shade Stalker
enemy.weakness: The Shade Stalker is immune to physical attacks but takes damage from sonic waves. The player must use their twin-bolt crossbow with the sonic-tipped bolts (from earlier) to harm it. Once hit by three sonic shots, it emits a ghostly cry and falls to the ground, revealing a hidden pool of liquid light that emits a low-frequency hum — the first step toward the final area.

encounters.hazard: The stalker can teleport behind the player using shadow-waves, which appear as flickers of darkness. The player must remain alert and use the crossbow’s sonic bolts to prevent it from reappearing.

pickup.name: liquid_light_pools
pickup.effect: The player can use this to activate dormant tree roots. When stepped on, it causes a brief illumination of the path ahead and emits a sound that echoes back — used in the final fight to trigger the boss's vulnerability.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Shade Stalker, the ground begins to vibrate. A faint pulsing sound emerges from the center — a hidden altar beneath the trees. The altar has a rune that glows only when the liquid light is used. If the player fails to collect it, they fall into a pit of silence and are teleported back to the first encounter, gaining 10 seconds of temporary invulnerability to discourage repeat attempts.

encounters.location: The Heartwood Chamber — a vast, circular clearing where ancient trees merge into a central pillar. Bioluminescent vines hang like curtains, and the air thrums with energy. At the center, a stone pedestal pulses with rhythm.

enemy.name: The Hollow Guardian
enemy.weakness: The Guardian is a massive, fused tree spirit that appears only at the heart of the jungle. It has three phases: dormant, aggressive, and final. In the final phase, it becomes vulnerable to a specific frequency — the hum of the 'crystallized root' when used in combination with the liquid light pool. The player must use both the crystallized root and the liquid light pool at the same time to activate a resonance pulse that damages the Guardian by 40% over 5 seconds. Without both, the Guardian attacks with a sonic wave that reduces the player’s health by 30%.

encounters.hazard: The Guardian emits sound waves that cause temporary deafness. The player must use the resonance pulse to break the silence and gain a brief vision of its inner form — a ghostly tree with a cracked heart.

pickup.name: resonance_frequency_tape
pickup.effect: This was a rare artifact found in the final encounter’s pool. It plays only when the player uses both the crystallized root and the liquid light pool together. The tape emits a deep, harmonic tone that triggers the Hollow Guardian's vulnerability. It is not usable by the player alone — it must be activated in tandem with the other two pickups. This is the player's final key to victory.

encounters.trigger: After successfully using the resonance pulse (requiring both the crystallized root and liquid light pool), the Guardian collapses into a still form. The final victory screen reveals a hidden map leading to a temple beyond the jungle — a hint of a greater world to explore.

boss.name: The Hollow Guardian (Final Form)
boss.weakness: The Guardian is vulnerable to a specific harmonic frequency — the 'resonance pulse' activated by combining the **crystallized root** (collected in Encounter 1) and the **liquid light pool** (collected in Encounter 2). This combination creates a sustained harmonic that damages the Guardian by 60% over 8 seconds. Without both pickups, the Guardian cannot be defeated and attacks with full force.
boss.victory_condition: The player must activate the resonance pulse at the correct moment during the final phase to deal critical damage. The game ends with a soft chime and a fading whisper: 'You hear the forest now.'

level.objective: Navigate the Whispering Canopy, defeat three enemies, collect key pickups, and activate the final resonance pulse to defeat the Hollow Guardian. The deeper the player goes, the more the jungle seems to watch — and remember.
level.reward: The 'Jungle Echo' amulet — a glowing device that allows the player to hear sounds in the jungle that were previously silent. It also unlocks a new ability: Sonic Step, which lets the player move silently while emitting a soft hum to detect enemies ahead.

level.theme: Tense, oppressive jungle with decaying vegetation and unnatural animal behavior
level.setting: The Whispering Mire — a forgotten stretch of jungle where the earth pulses with ancient energy. Trees grow in unnatural spirals. Mist clings to the canopy. The air hums with low-frequency vibrations. The jungle does not rest. It watches.

encounters.location: Swamp Trench - a narrow ravine with wet, crumbling stone walls. Vipers coil in shadows. The ground is unstable—step on a patch and it collapses into quicksand.

enemy.name: Swift Viper
enemy.weakness: Razorfang Dagger (player weapon) - cuts through scales and venom sacs. Critical hit on first strike inflicts bleeding (damage over 3 seconds).

encounters.hazard: Quick sand pits—step on one and the player is dragged down. Can only be pulled out by attacking the viper with Razorfang Dagger or using the Poison Dart.

pickup.name: Poison Dart (Shattered Root)
pickup.effect: Can be used to poison enemy attacks. When thrown, inflicts 15 damage over 5 seconds with a 20% chance to cause a panic reaction (enemy stops moving for 2 seconds). Must be used on the next enemy to be effective. Cannot be used if the player's health is below 60. Only one available per encounter.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Swift Viper, the jungle emits a low growl. A hidden cave entrance (covered in moss) splits open at the far end of the trench. If the player fails to kill the viper, the trench collapses and the player dies. The area becomes a dead zone, and the player is stuck in the trench forever (game over).

encounters.location: Cave of the Hollow Bones — a dark, winding cave with crumbling stalactites. The Warden patrols in tight corridors. The walls emit a low hum that increases enemy aggression every 30 seconds. Light flickers irregularly.

enemy.name: Gorge Warden
enemy.weakness: Poison Dart (Shattered Root) - when thrown at the Warden, it causes a 3-second paralysis. If used, the Warden's attack speed drops by 50%, and it takes 30% more damage. Must be used before the Warden detects the player (after 10 seconds of movement).

encounters.hazard: Stalactite collapse — after 10 seconds of inactivity, a ceiling beam drops. If the player is caught, they take 30 damage and are stunned. Must be in motion to survive.

pickup.name: Fang Trap (Lava-etched)
pickup.effect: A jagged, segmented trap that can be thrown. On impact, it creates a 4-second shockwave that damages all nearby enemies and causes a 1.5-second stun. It cannot be used within 2 seconds of being thrown. Can be used to disrupt the Warden’s movement or to create a safe zone in tight spaces. Only one available per encounter. Must be used during combat to activate its full effect.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Gorge Warden, a distant roar shakes the cavern. The jagged rock behind the cave wall shatters, revealing a fissure leading to a massive jungle chamber. If the player fails to kill the Warden, the trap collapses and the player is trapped in the cave with no path out. A second chance to fight is not available. The Warden’s death also causes the jungle to go silent for 10 seconds—before the final boss begins to stir.

encounters.location: Heart of the Mire — a massive, open clearing with a central stone monolith. The spirit stands atop it, eyes glowing red. The jungle is still. The air is thick with silence, broken only by distant animal howls. A golden spiral path leads to the monolith.

enemy.name: Ancient Jaguar Spirit
enemy.weakness: Fang Trap (Lava-etched) — when thrown directly at the Spirit’s eye (a glowing red pupil), it causes a 5-second stun and inflicts 70 damage. The Spirit will retreat and enter a passive state for 2 seconds. The trap must be thrown during a 3-second window after the Spirit’s next move. Only one trap available from prior encounter. Must be used before the Spirit reaches its final phase (which triggers a 200% damage buff).

encounters.hazard: Jungle Pulse — every 15 seconds, the jungle emits a shockwave that damages all players and enemies in a radius of 8. The pulse is strongest when the Spirit is in its final phase.

pickup.name: Fang Trap (Lava-etched)
pickup.effect: Used in final encounter to stun and damage the Jaguar Spirit. Must be used during a precise timing window. If not used, the Spirit enters a rage phase and attacks in 3-second bursts. The trap cannot be reacquired.

encounters.trigger: After the player defeats the Gorge Warden, the jungle stirs. The Spirit appears in the clearing. It does not attack immediately. After 15 seconds, it begins to charge. If the player fails to use the Fang Trap in time, the Spirit enters a rage phase and begins a 30-second attack cycle, dealing 120 damage per hit. The player must survive until the trap is used or die. No recovery. If the player dies during the fight, the jungle collapses, and the player is lost forever.

boss.name: Ancient Jaguar Spirit
boss.weakness: Fang Trap (Lava-etched) — must be thrown at the Spirit’s pupil during a 3-second window after its next movement. On success, the Spirit is stunned and takes 70 damage. This can be repeated up to 3 times before the Spirit enters full rage. The trap must be used before the Spirit reaches its final phase (which triggers 200% damage and immune to all attacks).
boss.victory_condition: The player must successfully use the Fang Trap at least twice to reduce the Jaguar Spirit's health below 200. After the final hit, the Spirit collapses and the jungle begins to heal. The player is rewarded with a rare artifact: 'The First Shadow Blade' (used to unlock a new class).

level.objective: Survive all encounters, using only the player’s rogue abilities and pickups. Each encounter builds tension and increases danger. The player must manage health, timing, and resource usage carefully. The final fight requires precise execution and memory of prior actions.
level.reward: First Shadow Blade — a cursed blade that can be used to cut through barriers or deal bonus damage to enemies with high health. Cannot be used without the player having successfully used the Fang Trap against the Jaguar Spirit before. Grants a +10% stealth bonus and a 2-second movement speed boost when used in combat.

level.setting: Lumina Grove – a serene, misty clearing at dawn. Sunlight filters through emerald canopies. A still pond reflects the sky. Vines drape gently from ancient trees. Birdsong and rustling leaves form a soft, peaceful background.

encounters.location: Near a mossy stone fountain at the edge of the clearing

enemy.name: Mist Wisp
enemy.weakness: Sunstone Stick (player's primary weapon). The Wisp is disoriented when struck by direct contact or beam from the stick, causing it to drift and fade.

encounters.hazard: Mist Wisp emits a soft fog that slows player movement if not moving in a straight line.

pickup.name: Moonbloom Leaf
pickup.effect: When held, allows player to walk on water and move slightly faster. Can be used to calm nearby wildlife. Can be planted later to grow Moonbloom Seed (essential for boss).

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Mist Wisp, the stone fountain gently opens, revealing a reflective pool of water. A soft chime echoes. The Moonbloom Leaf appears floating on the surface.

encounters.location: On the surface of the reflective pool, near a willow tree

enemy.name: River Glimmer
enemy.weakness: Moonbloom Leaf (pickup from previous fight). The Glimmer reflects and intensifies when exposed to the leaf. When the leaf is placed on or near it, the Glimmer flickers, becomes still, and dies in 2 seconds.

encounters.hazard: River Glimmer moves slowly and only activates when the player is near the water’s edge.

pickup.name: Moonbloom Seed
pickup.effect: When thrown into the pond, it activates a ripple effect. The pond lights up, and the Guardian of the Still Pond becomes vulnerable for 10 seconds. Must be thrown at the correct moment to trigger the boss fight.

encounters.trigger: After defeating River Glinmer, a vine-covered path opens from the willow tree. The path leads to the Ancient Grove, where a stone arch stands. The arch slowly reveals the Guardian of the Still Pond.

encounters.location: At the center of the Ancient Grove, a still pond surrounded by thorn vines and glowing moss

enemy.name: Guardian of the Still Pond
enemy.weakness: Moonbloom Seed (specific pickup from River Glimmer fight). The Guardian is inert until the seed is thrown into the central pond. Upon activation, it flickers and becomes vulnerable for 10 seconds, during which the player can strike it with any weapon. Only works once.

encounters.hazard: The Guardian remains still and calm. It does not attack directly. It only reacts to player proximity or the seed throw.

pickup.name: Moonbloom Seed
pickup.effect: As described above. Only obtained from defeating River Glimmer. Cannot be reused.

encounters.trigger: Appears only after player successfully completes the River Glimmer encounter. Requires Moonbloom Seed to be present and thrown into the pond to begin the fight. The fight begins only when the seed is activated.

boss.name: Guardian of the Still Pond
boss.victory_condition: Player must throw the Moonbloom Seed into the pond to activate the boss. Then, deal 100 damage to the Guardian using the Sunstone Stick or any weapon. The Guardian falls still, and the jungle renews with a soft glow.

level.objective: Reach the heart of Lumina Grove and awaken the Guardian of the Still Pond. Use the progression of nature and tools to defeat it in harmony with the jungle.
level.reward: The Moonbloom Bloom — a rare plant that grows in the garden after the fight. It restores 25% health and grants a passive ability: 'Harmony Walk' — increased movement speed while in peaceful zones.

level.setting: A forgotten necrotic hollow deep within the Shattered Canopy, where trees breathe in reverse, roots pulse with slow hearts, and the air hums with the whispers of dead flora. The jungle is decaying—vines coil like grasping hands, light filters through fog that clings like a shroud. A cold, metallic scent lingers. The ground is wet with blackened sap. Every footstep echoes in silence. The player, a necromancer, walks through the dead zones, summoning rot-wraiths and bones to navigate the darkness.

encounters.location: The Veil Chamber — a cave with a ceiling of hanging, blackened vines. The floor is slick with moss that glows faintly blue. A thick fog rolls in from a crack in the wall.

enemy.name: Warden of the Rotting Veil
enemy.weakness: Corrupted Bone Whip (player weapon) — causes immediate necrotic shock, draining 20% health and freezing the enemy for 2 seconds. Use this at full power to break its defense, or it will unleash a spreading rot-aura that spawns 2 rot-wraiths upon death.

encounters.hazard: Falling debris from above — triggers when enemy casts 'Flesh Spill' (a slow, creeping poison). If not avoided, causes 30% damage and 10 seconds of stagger.

pickup.name: Corrupted Bone Shard
pickup.effect: Can be used to counteract enemy attacks that drain life. When held, reduces all damage taken by 15% for 10 seconds. Also triggers passive ability: 'Bone Echo' — every time a necromancer spell is cast, a faint whisper echoes, hinting at the location of hidden threats. This pickup is dropped when the Warden is defeated and can be collected from a shattered bone pool beneath its body.

encounters.trigger: Upon defeating the Warden, the floor cracks open. A slow, pulsing root emerges and reveals a hidden passage behind a rotting log. This passage is blocked by the Rot-warden’s spawn point. The player must pass through to reach the next zone. If the player fails to reach it in 60 seconds, the rot-warden is awakened prematurely.

encounters.location: The Rotting Grove — a cavern of decaying trees, their trunks hollowed like skulls. A central tree pulses with a sickly green light. The air is thick with mold and the sound of slow, grinding roots.

enemy.name: Rot-warden (Phase 1)
enemy.weakness: Corrupted Bone Shard (pickup from previous encounter) — when used, the Rot-warden’s rot-aura is inverted. The enemy turns into a slow-moving husk for 4 seconds, and all decay effects reverse. If the player holds the shard and attacks, it deals 30% bonus necrotic damage and causes a 3-second paralysis to its core. This is the only way to defeat it in this phase.

encounters.hazard: Rotting roots — if stepped on, they activate and spawn a temporary swarm of bone-dust that stings for 2 seconds. Player can only step on them if wearing the Corrupted Bone Shard (this is a trigger for the next encounter).

pickup.name: Flicker Mask (Whispering)
pickup.effect: Activates after defeating the Rot-warden. When worn, the player gains vision of hidden enemies and can see future 5-second actions (like an enemy’s next attack). This is critical for anticipating boss spawns. The mask emits a low, harmonic tone — like a dying harp. It can be used in the final encounter to predict the boss’s movement patterns.

encounters.trigger: If the player defeats the Rot-warden, the central tree splits open. A new, pulsing core emits light and a low vibration. The screen dims. After 30 seconds, the core begins to hum. This is the pre-boss signal. The player is now tracked by a shadow entity — the 'Jungle Wailing Maw' — and must enter the core chamber to confront it. Failure to do so results in a 20-second timer where the player is isolated, and the Maw begins to manifest in the background.

encounters.location: The Core Chamber — a hollowed tree at the heart of the jungle. Walls are lined with ancient, half-burnt stone. A large, pulsating eye glows in the center. The air vibrates. The floor is made of black moss that pulses in sync with the Maw’s heartbeat.

enemy.name: Jungle Wailing Maw
enemy.weakness: Corrupted Bone Shard (specific pickup from Encounter 1) — if the player uses the Corrupted Bone Shard at full strength during its final phase, it causes a resonance cascade. The Maw's core fractures, and it emits a scream that triggers a reverse decay — all undead summoned by the player are instantly resurrected and attack it. This destroys its structure and ends the fight. The shard must be active in the player's hand to trigger this. If the shard is not present, the Maw evolves into a second phase (Phase 2) where it can regenerate health and summon a copy of the Rot-warden for 30 seconds. The player must survive 60 seconds without healing to survive Phase 2.

encounters.hazard: Maw Pulse — every 15 seconds, the chamber emits a shockwave that knocks back all enemies and deals 30% damage. If the player is not near the core, they are pushed to the edge, and falling into the gap below causes instant death.

pickup.name: Corrupted Bone Shard
pickup.effect: Specific pickup from Encounter 1. Used to weaken the Jungle Wailing Maw in the final phase. Only effective when used during direct combat. Must be equipped and actively used at full necromantic power to trigger the resonance cascade.

encounters.trigger: The Maw does not spawn immediately. It activates only after the Rot-warden is defeated and the player enters the Core Chamber. The player must have the Corrupted Bone Shard to activate the final weakness. If the player fails to obtain it, or uses it too late, the Maw enters Phase 2 and the encounter becomes unsolvable in 90 seconds.

boss.name: Jungle Wailing Maw
boss.weakness: Corrupted Bone Shard (from Encounter 1) — must be used during the final phase. If used, the Maw fractures, its core collapses, and the player wins. This is the only way to beat it without suffering massive damage. If not used, the Maw enters Phase 2 and can summon two Rot-wardens and spawn a corruption field that drains the player’s health over time.
boss.victory_condition: The Corrupted Bone Shard is used to trigger resonance cascade. This must happen within 30 seconds of the Maw’s final phase. After the cascade, the player gains a new ability: 'Eternal Bone Recall' — allowing them to resurrect one summoned creature instantly with no cost. This ability lasts 1 minute post-victory.

level.objective: Defeat the Jungle Wailing Maw using the Corrupted Bone Shard from the first encounter. Each enemy must be defeated using a specific weakness tied to the player's weapon or a pickup from a prior encounter. Failure to obtain the shard results in a permanent game over state.
level.reward: Eternal Bone Recall (passive ability), and a special necromantic relic: the 'Heart of the Shattered Canopy' — can be used to summon a permanent guardian spirit (a warden in player form) for one hour during gameplay. This is a major progression milestone.

level.setting: A vibrant, sun-dappled jungle filled with floating flowers, rainbow frogs, and talking trees. The air hums with magic. The ground is covered in mossy paths, and the trees have glowing vines that pulse with color. There are hidden glades, bubbling springs, and crystal mushrooms that emit soft light.

encounters.location: Sunlit Glade near the entrance

enemy.name: Bouncy Glimmermoss Gnat
enemy.weakness: Player's weapon: Glowing Alchemical Flask (causes a brief burst of sparkle that blinds the enemy for 1 second).

encounters.hazard: A slow-moving, giggling pond. Stepping in makes the player's feet glow for 3 seconds (good for attracting attention).

pickup.name: Sunbeam Tincture (Bottled)
pickup.effect: When used, gives the player +5 attack power and +10% chance to cause a harmless sparkle effect (affects enemies with a 30% chance). This sparkles can confuse small enemies for 1 second. Can be used on any enemy or in combat. Used in next encounter.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Glimmermoss Gnat, the player finds a hidden crystal mushroom that emits a soft glow. The mushroom pulses once, then opens to reveal a path leading to a hidden glade where the next enemy waits. This glade is marked by a floating sign that says: 'Next: The Whispering Leaf Frog!'

encounters.location: The Whispering Glade (activated by previous encounter)

enemy.name: Whispering Leaf Frog
enemy.weakness: Sunbeam Tincture (when used, the frog’s voice turns into static, and it becomes disoriented for 2 seconds).

encounters.hazard: A vine that swings slowly. If the player steps too close, it makes a 'whoosh' sound and briefly causes a harmless bounce effect (good for movement).

pickup.name: Mossy Sparkle Dust
pickup.effect: When scattered, causes a small area to sparkle with harmless light. Can be used to distract enemies or cause them to briefly freeze (1 second). Can be used in the final boss fight to weaken the boss’s defenses. Also, when combined with the Sunbeam Tincture, it enhances the sparkle effect (used in boss fight).

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Whispering Leaf Frog, a nearby tree drops a small, glowing seed. If the player picks it up, it sprouts into a floating mushroom that reads: 'The final danger lies beyond the storm pool. But beware — the storm pool is guarded by the Jungle Maw.' This sets up the final encounter (boss).

encounters.location: Storm Pool at the Jungle's Center

enemy.name: Jungle Maw (Boss)
enemy.weakness: Mossy Sparkle Dust (when used in the player's inventory, causes the Maw to emit a bubble of static, making it freeze for 3 seconds). The Maw is not harmed, but its movement and attack are disabled temporarily, allowing the player to deal damage safely. This is a direct result of the 'Mossy Sparkle Dust' pickup from the second encounter.

encounters.hazard: A bubbling, gentle storm pool. The water reflects the sky and occasionally shoots tiny sparkles upward (harmless).

pickup.name: Mossy Sparkle Dust
pickup.effect: As above — used to freeze or distract the boss during battle. This is the key weakness for the final fight.

encounters.trigger: The player arrives at the storm pool. A large, glowing mouth-shaped rock appears. The Jungle Maw slowly opens its eyes. The player is given a final warning: 'Only the sparkles can calm my hunger.' This refers to the Sparkle Dust collected earlier. If the player uses the Sparkle Dust, the Maw becomes vulnerable. The fight begins only after the player has used the Sparkle Dust in the combat menu.

boss.name: Jungle Maw (Boss)
boss.weakness: Mossy Sparkle Dust (from the second encounter pickup)
boss.victory_condition: Deal 150 damage with the Sparkle Dust active (causes 3-second freeze) and 3 successful attacks during the freeze window or after the freeze. Victory is achieved once the Maw's health reaches zero. A magical rainbow curtain appears after victory, and a new alchemical recipe is unlocked: 'Sparkle Infusion' (creates a permanent sparkle effect for 10 seconds).

level.objective: Find all three enemies and defeat the Jungle Maw. Use alchemical knowledge and the items collected from earlier encounters to overcome each threat. The journey is fun, full of playful surprises, and rewards curiosity.
level.reward: Alchemist's Sparkle Tome (unlocks new potion recipes, including temporary invisibility and minor healing from sparkling plants).

level.setting: A cursed, time-distorted jungle with flickering bioluminescent plants, slow-moving shadows, and broken time markers that pulse erratically. The air hums with a low, dissonant frequency, and moments of silence feel longer than they should—like time itself is breathing.

encounters.location: The Veil Clearing – a dense, fog-shrouded grove with twisted trees that appear to grow backwards. Bioluminescent fungi pulse in slow, irregular rhythms. A single broken clock ticks in reverse.

enemy.name: Time-Bound Warden
enemy.weakness: Chrono-Pulse (time-slowing effect) reduces Warden's movement speed by 75% and makes it vulnerable for 3 seconds, during which it takes 1.5x damage per hit. This ability is active when the player uses the Chrono-Pulse weapon in its base form (without any pickups). *Note: The Warden moves in cyclical loops. If the loop is broken, it becomes disoriented for 5 seconds.

encounters.hazard: Fog traps players if they move too slowly. If the fog reaches the player, their movement is reduced by 60% and vision becomes foggy for 3 seconds.

pickup.name: Time Shard
pickup.effect: Slows time around player by 50% for 10 seconds (max 3 uses). This is not a passive effect and must be activated manually via a short button press. Slows time only for the player and immediate area; enemies are unaffected by the time slowdown unless they are in the player’s field of view and actively moving.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Warden, the fog begins to thicken and the clock resets. A temporal ripple spreads outward, revealing a hidden cave entrance behind a wall of solidified time. The player must enter the cave to reach the next encounter. If the player fails to defeat the Warden within 60 seconds, the fog consumes the clearing and the player is teleported to a time-looping riverbank (reset). This adds a time-pressure element.

encounters.location: The Echoing Cave – a cavern with fractured time-stones that emit pulsing light. The walls appear to shift in reverse. The Watcher appears in three mirrored forms, each with a 1-second delay between them.

enemy.name: Shattered Watcher
enemy.weakness: Time Shard (must be used within 1 second of enemy attack). When the player uses the Time Shard during an enemy attack, the Watcher’s echoes freeze for 3 seconds. This breaks all duplicates, and the Watcher becomes vulnerable for 4 seconds. If used outside of the window, the Watcher gains 20% increased damage and 10% movement speed for 5 seconds as a counter-attack.

encounters.hazard: Time echoes cause the environment to flicker. If a flicker lasts longer than 2 seconds, the player is momentarily stuck in a loop of the last 3 seconds of movement.

pickup.name: Fossilized Second
pickup.effect: Rewinds the player's last action by exactly 1 second. Cannot be used to undo damage or death. Can be used once per encounter. Must be used during a moment of active combat (e.g., during an enemy attack). If used outside combat, it has no effect.

encounters.trigger: Defeating the Shattered Watcher causes the cave to collapse in a time loop. The collapse triggers a 30-second temporal rift that shows a distorted version of the jungle with a large, still figure in the center. After the rift closes, the player is teleported to a still field. A single glowing eye opens in the center. This is the final location — the Still Pulse's domain. The player must enter this field to reach the boss. If the player fails to defeat the Watcher within 90 seconds, the cave resets and the player returns to the Veil Clearing.

encounters.location: The Still Field – a vast, silent clearing with no wind, no sound, and no movement. The ground appears frozen in time. A single, massive figure — The Still Pulse — stands in the center. It emits a low-frequency pulse that causes all nearby objects to slow by 50%, and when it moves, it creates a ripple of distortion that lasts 4 seconds. The field is stable only if the player uses the Fossilized Second during a pulse.

enemy.name: The Still Pulse
